name: PRISM
description: The PRISM Alignment Dataset collects direct human interaction data and preference judgments from participants across 75 countries with diverse demographics, benchmarking 20+ LLMs on subjective and multicultural alignment. Reveals that human alignment preferences vary fundamentally across cultures, languages, and value systems — and that models trained primarily on English/Western data do not align with global human diversity.
evaluation_method: human preference judgments; alignment scores across demographic groups
general_score_metric: human preference rate; cross-cultural alignment consistency
typical_sota_score: Models show significant cross-cultural misalignment — preferences differ by up to 30–40% across cultural groups
reputation: Won NeurIPS 2024 Best Paper Award (Datasets & Benchmarks Track); most geographically diverse alignment dataset; fundamental challenge to universal alignment assumptions; 75 countries represented
notes: Won NeurIPS 2024 Best Paper Award in the Datasets & Benchmarks Track. Core finding: alignment is not universal — the same model response can be preferred in one cultural context and rejected in another. 75 countries represented, with careful demographic stratification. Challenges the assumption that a single aligned model can serve global users. Participatory design involved local researchers from each region.
